prize_parts.citation: for the prediction of flat bands in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated and superconducting states at the magic angle, opening moire quantum matter

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is a rare complete story: a quantitative prediction (the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model giving flat bands at a specific twist angle) followed by an experiment that found correlated insulators and superconductivity there, and then by independent reproduction in many laboratories and in many moire systems. It shows that experiment can still surprise theory, since nobody expected a tunable platform with Mott-like insulators and superconductivity in a single carbon-based device. The central observations are stable even though the pairing mechanism is not. The link between calculation and measurement is the kind I value, and the field has already opened routes to fractional Chern insulators and other moire phases, so the discovery has reach beyond one material. The credited trio gives a natural theory-plus-experiment split and is compatible with the three-person limit.
statement.case_against: The experimental discovery is only about eight years old, the origin of the superconductivity is still debated, and sample-to-sample and twist-angle disorder complicate reproducibility. The credit is also not airtight: Cao, Fatemi and the other first authors, Dean and Young for hBN-encapsulated moire work, and other early twisted-bilayer theorists lie outside the credited names. A committee that wants a settled microscopic understanding before awarding would reasonably wait, and the mature, cleanly attributed B012 would then be the safer choice.

responses.point: Mehlig ranked B057 first for its clean Z2 mechanism and a theory-plus-experiment pairing, while rating B036 as somewhat early because the interpretation of the superconductivity is unsettled.
responses.response: I agree that the pairing mechanism is open, but I do not think the prize must rest on it. The discovery to be credited is the flat-band prediction and the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity at the magic angle, and that part is reproduced and stable. I take his attribution point on B057 more seriously than my own ranking at the opening did: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are missing, and I find the HgTe credit gap harder to repair than the Cao and Dean questions around B036. The 2016 topological prize also leaves less new ground for B057 than B036 has relative to the 2010 graphene prize.

responses.point: Olsson ranked B036 third, considering the experimental discovery about eight years old and the superconducting phase still debated, and she put the MgO tunnel magnetoresistance prize (B005) second, proposing only the two experimentalists.
responses.response: The age is a fair concern, but eight years with hundreds of independent reproductions is not the same as a thin record, and the field has since produced several further phases. On B005 I agree that the experiments by Yuasa and Parkin are decisive, but I would keep Butler in, because the symmetry-filtering prediction is the physics and the electronic-structure link is what distinguishes this from an incremental follow-up to the 2007 GMR prize. I still rank it below B036 because of that overlap and because the weight is as much device engineering as discovery.

responses.point: Kroll and Lindroth both put the optical lattice clock (B012) first, as a precise, field-opening measurement method with a clean two-person credit.
responses.response: I accept that B012 has the cleanest attribution and the most mature confirmation on the shortlist, and I would be comfortable with it. My reservation is smaller than a disagreement: the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 prize on ion control cover neighbouring ground, and the lattice clock is a method that improves a measurement more than it reveals a new state of matter. I do not see opening support as a measure of scientific merit, so I keep B036 first, but I name B012 as my first alternative.

responses.point: Johansson ranked B036 sixth and deferred to condensed-matter colleagues, noting that credit for Cao, Dean and others is unresolved and that recognition may be slightly premature.
responses.response: I take the credit concern seriously and will not pretend the trio is complete. The prediction rests with Bistritzer and MacDonald, and the 2018 experiment came from Jarillo-Herrero's group, where the work was led by the group leader. That is a defensible allocation under the three-person limit, but the committee should check the experimental record before the final round. On timing I disagree mildly: the field is large enough and independently tested enough that waiting would not add much confidence in the central discovery.

uncertainties: Whether the unresolved pairing mechanism for superconductivity makes the discovery too early for the committee's standard.
Whether the experimental credit should be checked against Cao, Fatemi and other first authors, and Dean and Young for related work, who are outside the credited names.
Whether Bistritzer should be included alongside MacDonald or the theory share should be limited to one person.
How much weight the committee should give B012 over B036 given its much broader opening support and cleaner attribution.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile. I work in electronic-structure theory and magnetism at Uppsala, and have no stated personal or institutional link to MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer, Katori, Ye or the other shortlisted candidates, although I am close in field to the condensed-matter candidates and have a link to theory-experiment work at neutron and synchrotron facilities.
